# k0rdent_subnet (Resource)

A CIDR block allocated inside a `k0rdent_network` from a regional AddressPool.

**Every attribute replaces the subnet.** The API offers no update operation, so a change to anything, a display name included, is a destroy and recreate with a new CIDR. `exclude_ranges` is compared as addresses, so writing the same addresses another way is not a change. The API does not report `allocate_gateway`, so after an import that cannot infer it, the first apply records the configured value in place.

Subnets created by a cluster are not managed here. They carry a `cluster_id`, and `DELETE` against one answers `409`.

Requires `region` and `project` on the provider.

**What replaces it.** Changing `address_pool`, `allocate_gateway`, `description`, `display_name`, `exclude_ranges`, `id`, `network`, `prefix_length`, `project` or `region` cannot be done in place and replaces the subnet. A subnet holds the address allocation the workloads on it use. The API has no update for a subnet, so any change deletes it and allocates a new one from the pool, which can get a different CIDR and gateway. So a plan that would replace it fails and names the attribute, unless `allow_replace = true` is set on the resource. Everything else changes in place.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# One address, such as a control-plane VIP. A /32 has no gateway.
resource "k0rdent_subnet" "api_vip" {
  id      = "api-vip"
  network = k0rdent_network.training.id

  address_pool  = "/v1/regions/us-texas-1/networking/address-pools/tenant"
  prefix_length = 32
}

output "api_vip" {
  value = k0rdent_subnet.api_vip.cidr
}
```

```terraform
resource "k0rdent_subnet" "pods" {
  id      = "pods"
  network = k0rdent_network.training.id

  address_pool  = "/v1/regions/us-texas-1/networking/address-pools/tenant"
  prefix_length = 24

  # Sets `gateway` to the last usable address, if the pool is routable.
  allocate_gateway = true

  exclude_ranges = ["10.0.0.10-10.0.0.20"]
}

# The platform picks the CIDR.
output "pod_cidr" {
  value = k0rdent_subnet.pods.cidr
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `address_pool` (String) URI of the regional AddressPool the CIDR is allocated from. Must resolve in the network's region. **Forces replacement** (needs `allow_replace = true`).
- `network` (String) Id of the parent `k0rdent_network`. A subnet cannot move between networks. **Forces replacement** (needs `allow_replace = true`). **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.
- `prefix_length` (Number) Prefix length to allocate, within the pool's `[minPrefixLength, maxPrefixLength]`. `/31` is the RFC 3021 point-to-point case and `/32` the single-host case, such as a control-plane VIP. When the pool and this are known at plan, a value outside the pool's range, or larger than any prefix it holds, fails the plan. The pool doesn't report its free space, so a pool too full for this size still fails at create. **Forces replacement** (needs `allow_replace = true`). **Constraints:** Value must be between 1 and 32.

### Optional

- `allocate_gateway` (Boolean) Ask the platform to populate `gateway` with the last usable host address. Only takes effect when the AddressPool is routable. **Can force replacement** (needs `allow_replace = true`): replaces the subnet when it changes. The platform doesn't report it, so after importing a subnet on a pool that isn't routable the provider can't tell what it was, and the first apply records the configured value without replacing anything. Defaults to `false`.
- `allow_replace` (Boolean) Permit a plan that replaces this subnet. Left out or `false`, a change that cannot be made in place fails the plan, naming the attribute that forces the replacement, instead of destroying the subnet and creating another. Set it to `true` in the same configuration as the change to let the replacement go ahead, and remove it afterwards to put the guard back. It is read from the configuration being planned and must be known at plan time. It is never sent to the platform: setting or removing it on its own is an update that changes nothing there.
- `description` (String) Free-form text describing it, for people to read. **Forces replacement** (needs `allow_replace = true`).
- `display_name` (String) Human-friendly name. The API has no update for a subnet, so even this can't change in place. **Forces replacement** (needs `allow_replace = true`).
- `exclude_ranges` (List of String) Addresses inside the allocated CIDR to keep out of host allocation. A single IP (`10.0.0.4`), a CIDR (`10.0.0.0/29`) or a range (`10.0.0.10-10.0.0.20`). Left out, it reports what the platform applied, and removing it from configuration keeps those addresses excluded. Set it to `[]` to clear them, which replaces the subnet. **Can force replacement** (needs `allow_replace = true`): replaces the subnet when the excluded addresses change.
- `id` (String) Subnet name. Omit it and the provider generates one, `tf-` and 16 hex digits, so that a create whose answer is lost can be read back rather than sent twice. **Forces replacement** (needs `allow_replace = true`). **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL. String length must be at most 63.
- `project` (String) Project this resource belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `project`. It's part of the resource's API path, so a resource can't move between projects. **Forces replacement** (needs `allow_replace = true`). **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.
- `region` (String) Region this resource lives in. Defaults to the provider's `region`. It's part of the resource's API path, so a resource can't move between regions. **Forces replacement** (needs `allow_replace = true`). **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) How long each operation may take before it fails. Each operation left out defaults to the provider's `operation_timeout`, which is `2h` unless the provider block or `K0RDENT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT` sets it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `cidr` (String) The allocated block, e.g. `10.0.1.0/24`. Chosen by the platform from the AddressPool and empty until the subnet is `active`.
- `cluster_id` (String) UID of the cluster that provisioned this subnet. Present only on subnets the cluster lifecycle owns, which cannot be written through this resource.
- `gateway` (String) The resolved gateway address, when `allocate_gateway` was set and the pool is routable. Null otherwise.
- `ip_version` (String) IP family of the allocated CIDR. IPv4 only, today.
- `self_link` (String) Platform-defined reference to this subnet.
- `state` (String) Lifecycle state as last read from the platform.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) Bounds the whole create, including the wait until the platform reports it ready. Left out, it defaults to the provider's `operation_timeout`, which is `2h` unless the provider block or `K0RDENT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT` sets it. **Constraints:** Must be a positive duration of hours, minutes or seconds, such as `45m`, `2h` or `1h30m`.
- `delete` (String) Bounds the whole destroy, including the wait until the platform reports it gone. Left out, it defaults to the provider's `operation_timeout`, which is `2h` unless the provider block or `K0RDENT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT` sets it. **Constraints:** Must be a positive duration of hours, minutes or seconds, such as `45m`, `2h` or `1h30m`.

## Timeouts

The `timeouts` block sets how long each operation may take before it fails:

- `create` (default `2h`). Bounds the whole create, including the wait until the platform reports it ready.
- `delete` (default `2h`). Bounds the whole destroy, including the wait until the platform reports it gone.

Each default is the provider's `operation_timeout`, which is `2h` unless the provider block or `K0RDENT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT` sets it. An operation the block leaves out takes that value, so raising `operation_timeout` raises all of them at once. A value of zero or less is refused at plan time rather than read as no limit.

A wait that runs out, or a run that is interrupted, stops nothing on the platform. A create that stops waiting fails, and Terraform taints the object: run `terraform untaint` on it and then `terraform apply`, which waits for the same object. A delete that stops waiting fails and stays in state, and the next `terraform destroy` waits for the same delete without sending another.

```terraform
resource "k0rdent_subnet" "example" {
  # ...

  timeouts {
    create = "45m"
    delete = "45m"
  }
}
```

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# The same address with each part named. Leave out region and project to
# use the provider's.
import {
  to = k0rdent_subnet.example
  identity = {
    region  = "us-texas-1"
    project = "cp-production"
    network = "training-fabric"
    id      = "pods"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (String) The resource's id.
- `network` (String) Id of the network this resource lives under.

#### Optional

- `project` (String) Project the resource lives in. Defaults to the provider's `project` on import.
- `region` (String) Region the resource lives in. Defaults to the provider's `region` on import.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# Takes every id form `terraform import` does. The network is part of the
# address. The first command below names the network, the second names the
# scope too.
#
# On a pool that isn't routable, the plan after an import may show an in-place
# update to allocate_gateway that changes nothing on the platform.
import {
  to = k0rdent_subnet.example
  id = "us-texas-1/cp-production/training-fabric/pods"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import k0rdent_subnet.example training-fabric/pods

terraform import k0rdent_subnet.example us-texas-1/cp-production/training-fabric/pods
```
